2.2.6.3-r10.burton_quote: diseases were either procured by Music, or mitigated

2.2.6.3-r2.burton_quote: to rear and revive the languishing soul, affecting not only the ears, but the very arteries, the vital and animal spirits, it erects the mind, and makes it nimble

2.2.6.3-r3.burton_quote: the most dull, severe and sorrowful souls
2.2.6.3-r3.translation: Music by its charm captivates (the more severe minds), etc.

2.2.6.3-r4.burton_quote: not only to expel the greatest griefs, but it doth extenuate fears and furies, appeaseth cruelty, abateth heaviness

2.2.6.3-r5.burton_quote: because the spirits about the heart take in that trembling and dancing air into the body, are moved together, and stirred up with it
2.2.6.3-r5.translation: the muscles are moved by the spirit, etc.

2.2.6.3-r6.burton_quote: trees pulled up by the roots

2.2.6.3-r7.burton_quote: Harts, Hinds, Horses, Dogs, Bears, are exceedingly delighted with it

2.2.6.3-r8.burton_quote: he took infinite delight in singing, dancing, music, women’s company, and such-like pleasures; and if thou (saith he) didst but hear them play and dance, I know thou wouldst be so well pleased with the object, that thou wouldst dance for company thyself, without doubt thou wilt be taken with it

2.2.6.3-r9.burton_quote: I am beyond all measure affected with music, I do most willingly behold them dance, I am mightily detained and allured with that grace and comeliness of fair women, I am well pleased to be idle amongst them
